scope: C1-Y Y08-Y09 private native region completion and accepted-prefix failure ownership
snapshot_qualification: Final static/shared builds and 13-case tests use this product source, patch set and tests. The final static build is incremental after the upload-order test correction; shared log contains the full rebuild. No product file changed between these runs and this commit. Receipt/registry/LOC edits do not trigger a rebuild or P1.
implementation: Move-only NativeWork retains a backend, native completion fence, device/loader and strong graph/buffer/input lease through retirement.
The normal asynchronous path attaches completion to the original final compute batch. Original fusion and batching remain intact. Serial/diagnostic paths may append one region marker.
Failure and pending ownership are distinct. After a failed partial submit, poll does not block; wait drains actual upstream queues under their native locks. Observation/drain OOM retains owners.

Quiescence or device loss permits cleanup; unsubmitted contexts are discarded before backend teardown. The first error is preserved and failed slots are not reused. Destruction is a last-resort blocking drain.
Existing public route pending ownership, Direct/Graph lowering and cold graph/storage planning are unchanged in this slice.

build.runtime_environment: PATH unset, required DLLs beside EXE, system vulkan-1.dll, Khronos validation requested and explicit validation instance exercised

correctness_contract.region: Upstream F32 RMSNorm -> scale -> SiLU -> residual; existing rows 1/17/128 plus two independent 2048-wide asynchronous slots, each replayed with three varying inputs; independent double oracle tolerance 6e-6*(1+abs(expected)).
correctness_contract.slot_lifetime: Both inputs are uploaded before either slot is submitted. Strong leases remain until wait proves completion; duplicate submit is rejected. Moving and destroying a pending owner drains before its last graph lease disappears.
correctness_contract.partial_acceptance: Real Vulkan PFN wrappers reject the second submit of a 256-add region after an actual accepted prefix. Failed drain keeps buffers/memory live. Successful drain preserves the first error, submits no residual encoding, rejects reuse, and all tracked native handles return to zero.
correctness_contract.observation_failure: A real SiLU submission is followed by an injected fence-observation OOM and a separate queue-drain OOM. Poll remains nonblocking, owners remain live, later successful drain retires without resubmission.
correctness_contract.normal_completion_cost_observation: Both W1 result files record region_empty_submits=0; normal region submit makes no queue-idle call. This is a structural assertion, not P1.
correctness_contract.validation: No VUID in either final log; explicit validation instance ran without skip. Device-loss injection and serial/diagnostic fallback are not exercised in this slice.
correctness_contract.shared_test_boundary: NativeDevice/NativeWork ordinary and lease tests call the shared HYLE implementation. PFN fault tests use the same private vendor source linked into the test executable; they do not inject PFNs through the installed public DLL API.
correctness_contract.weights: Generated numeric fixture only; no actual checkpoint weights in this slice.

retained_failure: Initial MSVC compile rejected three ambiguous vk::Fence assignments from {}. Explicit nullptr fixed the handle reset; failure log retained. No algorithm correction or performance rerun.

p0.cold_cost: One backend and one additional completion fence per work slot; existing backend command/descriptor resources are retained across successful uses.
p0.execution_cost: One strong lease per region, stack TLS scope, pending/error bookkeeping and device-loss atomic loads. Original graph traversal/fusion/encoding and private allocations remain included. Native graph resources are recycled only after quiescence.
p0.failure_cost: Exceptional queue drain and final-destructor retry may block; normal poll never drains. Public abandonment must use the route pending owner during Y4 integration.
